From c381039ade2e161ab08c0eda73c4f8b9a7115928 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Wyatt Feng <bronzed_45_vested@icloud.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 00:46:27 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] xfrm: espintcp: do not reuse an in-progress partial send

espintcp keeps a single in-flight transmit in ctx->partial.
Before building a new sk_msg, espintcp_sendmsg() first tries to flush
that state through espintcp_push_msgs().

For blocking callers, espintcp_push_msgs() may return success even when
the previous partial send is still pending. espintcp_sendmsg() would
then reinitialize emsg->skmsg and reuse ctx->partial while the old
transfer still owns that state.

Do not rebuild the send message when ctx->partial is still in progress.
If espintcp_push_msgs() returns with emsg->len still set, fail the new
send instead of overwriting the live partial state.

This is a memory-safety fix: reusing the live partial-send state can
leave a stale offset attached to a new sk_msg and lead to an out-of-
bounds read in the send path.

tcp_sendmsg_locked() already handles waiting for send buffer memory, so
the fix here is just to preserve espintcp's one-message-at-a-time
transmit state.

Fixes: e27cca96cd68 ("xfrm: add espintcp (RFC 8229)")
Cc: stable@kernel.org
Reported-by: Yuan Tan <yuantan098@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Yifan Wu <yifanwucs@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Juefei Pu <tomapufckgml@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Zhengchuan Liang <zcliangcn@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Xin Liu <bird@lzu.edu.cn>
Assisted-by: Codex:GPT-5.4
Signed-off-by: Wyatt Feng <bronzed_45_vested@icloud.com>
Signed-off-by: Ren Wei <n05ec@lzu.edu.cn>
Signed-off-by: Steffen Klassert <steffen.klassert@secunet.com>

diff --git a/net/xfrm/espintcp.c b/net/xfrm/espintcp.c
index a2756186e13a..d9035546375e 100644
--- a/net/xfrm/espintcp.c
+++ b/net/xfrm/espintcp.c
@@ -346,6 +346,10 @@ static int espintcp_sendmsg(struct sock *sk, struct msghdr *msg, size_t size)
 			err = -ENOBUFS;
 		goto unlock;
 	}
+	if (emsg->len) {
+		err = -ENOBUFS;
+		goto unlock;
+	}
 
 	sk_msg_init(&emsg->skmsg);
 	while (1) {
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### File: `net/xfrm/espintcp.c`

- **Added a new error check** after the existing `espintcp_push_msgs()` call in `espintcp_sendmsg()`.  
  Specifically, inserted the following code:
  ```c
  if (emsg->len) {
      err = -ENOBUFS;
      goto unlock;
  }
  ```
  This checks whether the partial send state (`ctx->partial`) is still in progress (indicated by `emsg->len > 0`). If a previous send is still pending, the function now returns `-ENOBUFS` and jumps to the `unlock` label instead of continuing to reinitialize and reuse the live partial state.

### Relationship to the Bug Fix

The original code could call `espintcp_push_msgs()` to flush a previously incomplete send (stored in `ctx->partial`). For blocking sockets, this call could return success even when the partial send was not yet fully transmitted to the TCP layer. The function then proceeded to reinitialize `emsg->skmsg` and build a new message, effectively overwriting `ctx->partial` while the old transfer still owned that state. This reuse of live partial-send state could lead to stale offsets and out-of-bound reads in the subsequent send path.

The added check prevents this by explicitly refusing to build a new message if the previous partial send has not completed (`emsg->len != 0`), ensuring that `espintcp` only handles one message at a time and never overwrites an in-progress transmit. This preserves the integrity of the partial-send machinery and fixes the memory-safety vulnerability.
